items.title: Ed Polcer interviewed by Monk Rowe, Tarrytown, New York, October 31, 1998
items.q: Stan went to play at Grace Kelly’s wedding

ctx.x: It was like story book. I mean I didn’t know Princeton and the Ivy League tradition and anything like that. I mean I was never caught up in it. I never thought I’d go to an Ivy League school. We couldn’t afford it. So it was never a thing. All I knew is when I was a kid Dick Hasmeier played football and was all-American and played, and that was Princeton. And every Saturday when I was in high school, Ted Huesing, the radio disc jockey, had a thing called, well he had “Ted Heusing’s Bandstand” on WNEW or WINS…

was playing a Dixieland jazz thing and playing very hot, saying somebody’s going to hear me. And the first time I tried this, I wasn’t doing it for more than about a half an hour and suddenly I get a knock on the door. It wasn’t Stan Rubin, but it was one of his competitors, Dennis Brady, who had the Nassau Jazz Band, and it took that long for him to ask me to become his cornet player. Stan Rubin heard us, Stan Rubin booked us in Carnegie Hall along with his band, he had the Nassau Jazz Band play a couple of…
